title: Atoll Healthcare partner seed notes
content:
Goal: quick pilot with Atoll (regional telehealth provider) to validate Redwood Private for protected PHI inference and prove cost/latency targets for conversational triage assistant. Short, low-risk kickoff: 6-week scoped pilot + decision meeting.

Background notes (what I found):
- Atoll Healthcare: mid-sized regional network (east coast), proprietary teletriage product used by 40 clinics, ~80k monthly unique patients. Recent exec hire: Head of Digital, Eloise Tan (LinkedIn: eloise.tan).
- Existing stack: Node-based backend, mix of AWS-hosted infra and some on-prem for imaging PHI. They use a third-party transcription vendor and an internal rules engine for triage flows.
- Pain: long wait times during peak hours; clinicians spending ~4–6 minutes per triage interaction on record cleanup and summarization. Security posture: strong; require SOC2 certified partner and private networking.
- Decision makers: Head of Digital (Eloise), CTO (Marcus Reeves), Security lead (Anita Chow). Procurement starts if legal OK with private deployment + BAA.

Pilot hypothesis / success metrics (proposed):
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end response <= 350ms for short prompts (triage completion step) on dedicated/private infra.
- Cost: token cost reduction target vs current SaaS LLM (benchmark provided during scoping).
- Quality: clinical summary accuracy within 90% agreement to clinician label on 50 curated cases (scoped eval set).
- UX: average clinician time saved >= 2 min per triage.

Proposed pilot scope (6 weeks, minimal legal):
- Week 0: NDA + BAA, initial kickoff, narrow dataset definition (50 de-identified transcripts).
- Week 1: Redwood Private quickstart in Atoll VPC (control plane hosted, inference in VPC), ingestion pipeline for de-identified transcripts, baseline eval vs current vendor.
- Week 2–3: Model tuning & prompts, run 50-case eval, run A/B internal small-sample clinician review (5 clinicians).
- Week 4: Performance tuning (batching + KV caching configs), latency tests across clinics, cost estimates for 10k/mo active users.
- Week 5: Roll demo to 1 clinic (shadow mode), collect clinician time metrics.
- Week 6: Consolidate results, ROI/cost model, decision meeting with stakeholders.

Technical/ops notes (quick sketch):
- Preference: Redwood Private (because of PHI). Offer both options but prioritize Private BYO-VPC pattern to avoid full on-prem procurement.
- KMS: integrate with Atoll KMS (they use Azure KeyVault) — checklist: service principal, key policy for envelope encryption.
- Network: need peering + restricted egress; mention NAT requirement.
- Observability: propose 30d trace logs (token-level cost disabled for PHI), provide metrics dashboard screenshots from similar pilot (internal link).
- Data handling: de-identification step mandatory; propose joint script (we provide a starter python de-id notebook).

Value messaging (for outreach):
- Speed + cost: predictable dedicated capacity without vendor lock-in; show 30–40% per-token saving via batching & quantized variants for non-critical generation.
- Compliance: Private deployment options + BAA; audit logs and KMS integration.
- Clinician UX: shorter notes, structured summaries ready for EHR copy-paste.

Cold outreach variants (A/B test subject lines + short pitch):
- Subject A: "Pilot idea: cut clinician triage time at Atoll by 30% (6-week pilot)"
  Body (short): "Hi Eloise — quick idea: help Atoll reduce clinician triage time by ~2–3 minutes using a private LLM deployment. We run a 6-week pilot (BAA-friendly) and deliver an apples-to-apples eval vs your current vendor. Interested in a 20-minute sync? — Samira"
- Subject B: "Private LLM pilot for teletriage (low risk, PHI-ready)"
  Body (short): "Eloise — we helped a similar regional network run a Private LLM pilot inside their VPC, hitting 95p latency <350ms and saving clinicians time. Can I share a one-page pilot plan?"
- Subject C (technical): "Quick question on Atoll's KMS + network for a Private LLM pilot"
  Body (short): "Marcus/Anita — do you run keys in Azure KeyVault? If so, we have a streamlined flow for envelope encryption and VPC peering that avoids egress. Short 15-min call to confirm requirements?"

Objection handling (short bullets):
- 'PHI risk': we require BAA; run in-customer VPC; disable token-level logging for PHI routes; KMS/HSM integration + audit logs.
- 'Cost unknown': show estimated cost model tied to active clinician minutes and sample invoices from similar pilot. Offer committed reserved cap for pilot to stabilize unit economics.
- 'Integration effort': ship de-id notebook + starter ingestion hooks (Node/Express example) — estimated 3–5 engineering days on Atoll side for a shadow integration.
- 'Model quality risks': scoped eval set + paired-review by clinicians — accept failure criteria and iterate prompts/quantized model variants.

Call prep (for first intro with Eloise):
- Objectives: confirm pilot appetite, map stakeholders, ask about PHI flows and procurement timeline, secure OK for de-id sample.
- Agenda (15–20m): 1) quick intros (2m) 2) problem fit & what success looks like (4m) 3) pilot outline + ask (5m) 4) technical constraints (3m) 5) next steps (1m).
- Key questions:
  - Who owns procurement for vendor BAAs?
  - Do you have a strict no-egress policy?
  - Which EHR(s) do you integrate with? Is FHIR used?
  - Approx clinician volume per clinic during peak? (helps model cost)

Internal ask / next actions (priority list):
1) Share this note with Solutions Eng (Diego) + Security (Priya) and ask for quick feasibility + rough infra checklist by EOD Wed.
2) Draft one-page pilot overview (I can draft; ask Solutions Eng for network/KMS blurb).
3) Prepare de-id example + Node ingestion snippet (Diego to own).
4) Prep ROI slide with 2 scenarios (conservative, optimistic) — request numbers from Sales Ops.

Quick pricing anchors (to mention, not final):
- Pilot pricing: $12k flat (6-week) + optional engineering support block (10 days @ $2.4k/day) — aim to keep low friction.
- Production: show both reserved capacity and pay-as-you-go; reserved capacity example: $X/month for N GPUs (we'll use internal calc later).

Notes-to-self (brain dump):
- If legal pushes back on hosted control plane, propose fully customer-managed control plane (longer but possible).
- Prepare a short case study from a similar customer (anonymized) to include in outreach.
- Run internal perf test on a 1-node private deployment for similar transcript lengths to validate latency claim.

Draft follow-up email (if no reply after 5 days):
"Eloise — following up on the pilot note. Happy to share a 1-pager and a short checklist for your security team. Quick yes/no?"

End of scratchpad.

----
Small attachments to prepare for next sync:
- 1-pager pilot PDF (one-paragraph value + timeline + ask)
- De-id notebook (python) + README.txt
- Node ingestion example (zip)
- Baseline perf sheet (sheet)
